newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges citizens to postpone travel to PNG.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges citizens to postpone travel to PNG.

text.p: The U.S. State Department on Tuesday advised American citizens to postpone all non-essential travel to Papua New Guinea because of threats against foreigners by insurgents in Bougainville province.
It said in a public announcement that the threats and other developments "could lead to civil disturbances in Bougainville or elsewhere in Papua New Guinea".
The anouncement gave no details of the threats.
Americans on Bougainville island, scene of a nine-year-old uprising, should leave immediately, it said, and others elsewhere in the country should defer all travel there.
All Americans in Papua New Guinea were urged to exercise caution and stay in regular touch with the U.S. embassy.
The prime minister of the South Pacific nation, Sir Julius Chan, said on Tuesday his government was in "absolute control" after the sacking of its rebellious army chief.
The officer, Brig.-Gen. Jerry Singirok, had given Chan and other ministers a 48-hour ultimatum to resign over their decision to use mercenaries against the Bougainville rebellion.
